parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Good evening. <short pause> Tonight's story is called The Shepherd's Lantern. <short pause> Before we begin, let your shoulders drop... and let the bed hold all of your weight.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Take one slow breath in... <short pause> and let it go. <short pause> There is nowhere you need to be now. <short pause> Nothing left to fix tonight. <short pause> Just listen, and let the story carry you.

Far away, in a land of soft brown hills, there lived an old shepherd named Eli. <short pause> His house was small and made of stone, with one window that looked toward the east. <short pause> And every evening, when the sun went down behind the hills, Eli took his lantern from its hook beside the door.

It was a plain lantern. <short pause> Iron, a little rusted at the edges, with a glass that had been cleaned so many times it had gone faintly cloudy. <short pause> But it gave a warm, honey-colored light... <short pause> and the sheep knew it the way children know their mother's voice.

parts.style: gentle, slow, painting a calm scene
parts.text: On this particular evening, the air was cool and still. <short pause> The last of the swallows had gone to their nests under the roof. <short pause> Somewhere down in the valley, a dog barked once, and then thought better of it. <short pause> Eli lit the wick with a small brass match, closed the little glass door, and stepped outside.

parts.style: gentle, slow, painting a calm scene
parts.text: The path to the high pasture was narrow and familiar. <short pause> He had walked it for more than fifty years, and his feet found every stone without needing to look. <short pause> The grass brushed against his ankles, damp with the first of the evening dew. <short pause> It smelled of thyme, and of earth, and of the long warm day now ending.

As he walked, Eli hummed an old song his father had taught him. <short pause> It had no real words... only a slow rising and falling, like breathing. <short pause> Up ahead, he could hear the sheep. <short pause> A soft bleat here. <short pause> The small bell on the lead ewe, ringing once, then again.

parts.style: gentle, slow, painting a calm scene
parts.text: At the top of the hill, the pasture opened wide beneath the sky. <short pause> The sheep were gathered close together near the old stone wall, pale shapes in the deepening blue. <short pause> When they saw the lantern coming, they lifted their heads... <short pause> and then, one by one, they lowered them again. <short pause> He was here. <short pause> All was well.

Eli counted them, as he always did. <short pause> Not quickly, but slowly, touching each one with his eyes. <short pause> Thirty-one, thirty-two, thirty-three... <short pause> all of them, every one. <short pause> Even the little brown lamb who liked to wander was there, tucked against her mother's side.

He set the lantern on a flat rock by the wall, where its light could spread across the grass. <short pause> Then he sat down on his old wool cloak, leaned his back against the cool stones, and rested his staff across his knees.

parts.style: gentle, slow, painting a calm scene
parts.text: Above him, the stars were coming out. <short pause> First one, low in the west, bright as a drop of silver. <short pause> Then a few more. <short pause> Then too many to count. <short pause> The sky seemed to grow deeper and wider, the way it only does in places far from any town.

Eli had often wondered how the One who made all those stars could also know the name of one old shepherd on one small hill. <short pause> And yet he believed it. <short pause> He had felt it, on nights like this one.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: He remembered the words his mother used to say to him at bedtime, when he was a small boy afraid of the dark. <short pause> I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety. <long pause>

A breeze moved through the pasture, soft as a hand passing over the grass. <short pause> The lantern flame leaned, and then stood straight again. <short pause> One of the sheep sighed in her sleep. <short pause> Far below, in the village, the last window went dark.

parts.style: gentle, slow, painting a calm scene
parts.text: Eli watched over them, as the night grew quieter. <short pause> He listened to the small sounds of the hillside. <short pause> The crickets in the wall. <short pause> The slow chewing of a ewe who was not quite ready to sleep. <short pause> The distant whisper of the stream at the bottom of the valley.

He was not worried. <short pause> He had done what a shepherd does. <short pause> He had walked the path. <short pause> He had counted his flock. <short pause> He had set his light where they could see it. <short pause> And now there was nothing left to do but to stay close, and keep watch, and rest.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: And perhaps you are a little like those sheep tonight. <short pause> Gathered in. <short pause> Counted. <short pause> Known by name. <short pause> You do not have to keep watch over the night yourself. <short pause> Someone kinder and stronger than any shepherd is already watching.

As the hours passed, the lantern burned lower. <short pause> Its light grew smaller and softer, until it was only a small golden glow on the rock. <short pause> Eli's eyes grew heavy. <short pause> He pulled his cloak a little closer around his shoulders.

parts.style: gentle, slow, painting a calm scene
parts.text: The stars turned slowly overhead, the way they had turned for a thousand years. <short pause> The grass was silver now with dew. <short pause> The little brown lamb was fast asleep. <short pause> Her mother was asleep. <short pause> The whole hillside was breathing slowly, all together, like one great quiet creature resting under the sky.

And Eli, the old shepherd, let his head rest back against the stones. <short pause> He thought of nothing in particular. <short pause> The warmth of the cloak. <short pause> The smell of the grass. <short pause> The light, still glowing, small and faithful, beside him.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let yourself be there with him now. <short pause> The cool air on your face. <short pause> The soft ground beneath you. <short pause> The stars above, and the quiet all around. <short pause> Breathe in slowly... <short pause> and breathe out.
Good Shepherd, <short pause> thank You that You never sleep, so that I can. <short pause> Watch over me through this night, <short pause> and keep the ones I love close to You. <short pause> Amen.
Rest now. <short pause> The lantern is lit. <short pause> The flock is gathered. <short pause> And you are safe. <short pause> Goodnight.
